title: Polar Station Pole-2
victim: Ignat Severov, head of the station
teaser: The nearest settlement is two hundred kilometres away, and the radio has been silent for three days. The head of the station went out to take a temperature reading and never came back from the snow by the weather box. Two sets of tracks led to the hut, and by everyone's account only one person came back.

habits.label: Frostbitten fingers
habits.habit: White frostbite patches on the fingers
clues: The frosted door of the weather box shows fingerprints with smooth pads and no pattern, as happens after frostbite. The culprit has frostbitten fingers.
A mitten hangs on a hook in the entry porch, its inside thickly smeared with goose fat against frostbite. The culprit has frostbitten fingers.

habits.label: Bone amulet
habits.habit: A walrus-tusk amulet around the neck
clues: A torn bit of rawhide cord with a crumb of bone was found in the snow by the weather box. The culprit wears a walrus-tusk amulet around their neck.
There's a handful of fresh walrus-ivory shavings on the workbench in the diesel room; someone recently touched up a carving. The culprit wears a walrus-tusk amulet.

habits.label: Smells of blubber
clues: Severov's jacket sleeve has a greasy stain that reeks of seal blubber. The culprit's clothes smell of blubber.
There's a dark, fishy smear of blubber on the door handle in the entry porch. The culprit's clothes smell of blubber.

habits.label: Dog hair
habits.habit: Clothes covered in grey dog hair
clues: There are tufts of grey dog hair on the threshold of the weather box, and the dogs were tied up by the shed all night. The culprit's clothes are covered in dog hair.
Grey dog hairs are stuck to the dead man's collar, though Severov hadn't been near the team for a week. The culprit's clothes are covered in dog hair.

habits.label: Scar on the cheekbone
habits.habit: A white scar across the cheekbone
clues: After four o'clock the radio operator saw a face with a white line across the cheekbone in the porch window. The culprit has a scar on their cheekbone.
In the margin of the observation log Severov sketched a profile with a scar across the cheekbone and a question mark. The culprit has a scar on their cheekbone.

habits.label: Tea through a sugar lump
habits.habit: Drinks tea through a lump of cracked sugar
clues: A bitten lump of cracked sugar lies next to a cold mug in the mess room, and the communal pot uses granulated sugar. The culprit sips tea through a sugar lump.
In the food store a fresh corner has been knocked off the sugar loaf, and crumbs glitter on the floor. The culprit sips tea through a sugar lump.

habits.label: Chess player
clues: An adjourned game stands on the board in the mess room, and the envelope with the sealed move is in the dead man's pocket. The culprit plays chess.
A radiogram form in the radio room has moves written on it: "e2-e4, Ng8-f6". The culprit plays correspondence chess.

habits.label: Plays the accordion
clues: At about five in the morning someone started playing the accordion in the mess room, and over the music nobody heard the porch door slam. The culprit plays the accordion.
There's melting snow on the bellows of the accordion in the mess room, as if it was picked up straight from the cold. The culprit plays the button accordion.

habits.label: Chews resin
clues: A lump of chewed larch gum is stuck to the threshold of the weather box. The culprit chews resin.
A tin of larch gum stands on the porch windowsill, and one piece has been bitten. The culprit chews resin.

habits.label: Anchor tattoo
habits.habit: A blue anchor tattooed on the wrist
clues: In the entry porch the cook saw a bare hand with a blue anchor on the wrist. The culprit has an anchor tattoo.
Severov's diary entry for yesterday reads: "Another row with the one who has the anchor on his hand." The culprit has an anchor tattoo.

habits.label: Beaded fur boots
habits.habit: Wears fur boots embroidered with beads
clues: A red bead from beadwork was found in the snow by the weather box. The culprit wears beaded fur boots.
The second set of tracks by the weather box is soft and heelless, with a patterned seam along the edge of the sole. The culprit wears fur boots embroidered with beads.

habits.label: Navigates by the stars
habits.habit: Finds their way by the stars
clues: The lamp on the path to the weather box was out, the night was moonless, and yet the trail runs dead straight without a single loop. The culprit navigates by the stars.
Someone drew the Plough with a finger on the misted glass in the ice lab, with an arrow to the weather box. The culprit finds their way by the stars.

habits.label: Skis well
clues: A fresh ski track runs from the weather box to the food store, smooth and with long glides. The culprit is an excellent skier.
A pair of skis stands in the entry porch with wet bindings and melting snow on the climbing skins. The culprit skis.

habits.label: Polar postmarks
clues: In the radio room the station postmarks have been neatly cut out of a pile of official envelopes. The culprit collects polar postmarks.
In the snow by the weather box there's a scrap of envelope stamped "Pole-2", cut out with scissors around the postmark. The culprit collects envelopes with polar postmarks.

habits.label: Racking cough
habits.habit: A deep cough left over from pneumonia
clues: The cook heard a deep, racking cough from the entry porch a minute before the door slammed. The culprit coughs all the time.
The radio room log has a note: "05:20, someone coughing under the window for a long time." The culprit coughs all the time.

habits.label: Red hair
clues: A few bright red hairs are caught in Severov's fur mitten. The culprit has red hair.
The night duty officer says the lamp by the weather box picked out a lock of red hair under a hat. The culprit has red hair.

tech: The thermograph in the weather box stopped at exactly 05:30, though its mainspring is intact. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
The radio has been silent for three days, and one valve has been neatly removed from the power unit. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
sched: Severov went out to the weather box strictly on the observation schedule, and that's exactly where someone was waiting for him. The culprit knows the schedule.
In the observation log, the 05:30 reading is circled in pencil. The culprit knows the schedule.
late: The light in the ice lab burned until morning, though the schedule says it's used only by day. The culprit doesn't sleep at night.
The night duty officer heard footsteps in the corridor after three, when the whole station is asleep. The culprit is a night owl.
tools: The weather box door was taken off its hinges and put back, the bolts tightened evenly. The culprit is handy with tools.
The flare-gun box in the entry porch was opened without a single scratch, with a screwdriver from the diesel room lying beside it. The culprit is handy with tools.
strong: Severov was dragged through deep snow from the porch to the weather box. The culprit is physically strong.
The iced-up barrel used to bar the weather box door can't be shifted by one person, yet it was rolled away. The culprit is physically strong.
medic: The doctor found no wounds on the body, but there's an odourless residue in Severov's thermos. The culprit knows about poisons.
A bottle of sleeping pills has vanished from the station's medicine chest, and the dose in the thermos was calculated exactly for Severov's weight. The culprit knows about poisons.
glasses: A lens in a thin metal frame lies in the snow by the weather box. The culprit wears glasses.
There are two round marks on the frosty windowsill of the radio room, as if glasses had been put down lenses first. The culprit wears glasses.
driver: During the night the snowcat was driven away from the diesel room and brought back, and its engine is still warm. The culprit can drive.
Fresh caterpillar tracks run from the garage to the weather box and back. The culprit can drive.
quiet: The sled dogs didn't bark once all night, though their kennels stand right by the path. The culprit moves silently.
The crust by the weather box crunches loudly, yet the duty officer in the porch didn't hear a single step. The culprit moves silently.
keys: The food store was opened during the night and padlocked again, without a scratch. The culprit had keys.
The radio room was opened with its own key, and its lock can't be picked. The culprit had keys.
cash: A quarter's polar allowances are missing from the quartermaster's drawer, yet the payroll is signed as it should be. The culprit had access to money.
A line about money paid out to send to the mainland has been erased from the store's account book. The culprit had access to money.
safe: The head of station's iron safe was opened without force, and the cipher notebook is gone. The culprit knows the safe combination.
Severov kept the combination in his head and never wrote it down, yet the safe was opened on the first try during the night. The culprit knows the safe combination.
french: Someone has added in the margin of the weather log: "Il ne reviendra pas". The culprit knows French.
A draft radiogram in French, addressed to a foreign expedition, was found in the entry porch. The culprit knows French.
